issues.description: Uses 'system' with 'rm -rf' for cleanup. While safe here with hardcoded paths, it's less portable than using Scheme-native file deletion if available.

files_reviewed.notes: Comprehensive test suite covering BFS, DFS, pathfinding, and graph metrics. Well-structured and uses a clear DAG for verification.

issues.description: map-collection throws an error if a block is missing, while fold-collection and filter-collection silently skip them. This inconsistency could lead to unexpected crashes in distributed environments.
collection-group-by has O(N^2) complexity due to nested map/assoc usage for each element. For large collections, this will be significantly slow.
collection-add and collection-merge do not check for duplicate hashes, which might lead to unexpected growth if called repeatedly with the same members.

files_reviewed.notes: Good set of functional primitives. The TIER assignment comments help with project navigation. Logic is mostly sound but performance for large collections is a concern.

issues.description: (cdr (assq 'body post)) will crash if a post is missing the 'body' field (assq returns #f). This occurs in multiple functions: find-tagged, list-all-tags, tag-histogram, etc.
count-occurrences is O(N^2) because it calls remove-assq inside a loop over the input list. Scalability issue for high tag counts.
Functions like find-tagged and tag-histogram call collect-all-posts on every invocation. In a large forum, this causes massive I/O overhead without caching.

files_reviewed.notes: Functional tag query system but lacks defensive programming for alist lookups. Performance will degrade quickly as the number of posts grows due to lack of indexing or caching.

summary: The graph algorithm tests are excellent. Collection utilities are solid but have some performance bottlenecks and inconsistencies in error handling. The query system is functional for small datasets but contains high-severity risks of crashing on malformed posts and has significant scalability concerns.
